message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills and modern scares you might enjoy for a Friday‑night movie marathon:

| # | Title | Year | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A masterclass in dread—Jack Nicholson’s descent into madness set against an isolated hotel. |
| 2 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart social thriller that blends horror with biting satire; perfect if you like something that makes you think as well as scream. |
| 3 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A slow‑burn psychological horror that escalates into a gut‑wrenching climax; great for fans of unsettling atmosphere. |
| 4 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Suspense built around silence—every footstep could be your last. |
| 5 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight nightmare that turns the usual tropes on their head; it’s both beautiful and brutal. |
| 6 | **It Follows** | 2014 | An inventive premise (a curse that follows you) paired with a creepy soundtrack; a fresh take on the supernatural genre. |
| 7 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A solid, spooky film that’s part of a larger universe—great if you want something more mainstream but still effective. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A psychological horror about grief that feels very personal and deeply unsettling. |
| 9 | **Suspiria** | 1977 | For those who love surreal visuals and a haunting score—this one is a cult classic. |
|10 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑horror that starts as a typical “camp‑fire” story and then flips the script. |

Feel free to shuffle them or pick a theme (e.g., “classic vs. contemporary”) to keep the night interesting!
